| [`E0040`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0040) | query without `key`, mutation with `stale`, or another invalid query argument |
| [`E0041`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0041) | query or mutation function with an invalid signature |
| [`E0042`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0042) | query whose success value is `()` or an `Option` |
| [`E0050`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0050) | duplicate type name, id or variant index |
| [`E0051`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0051) | a name that collides after case conversion or is not an identifier |
| [`E0052`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0052) | an item named like a standard library item, with another id |
| [`E0060`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0060) | a spelling that looks like a built-in Undra type is another type |
| [`E0061`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0061) | the name written is not the declared name of the type, or the type is not declared with `#[undra::api]` |
| [`E0062`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0062) | a port call could not be answered and its method has no error channel: a runtime message |
| [`E0063`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0063) | nested `Option<Option<T>>` |
| [`E0064`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0064) | an object (`#[undra::api] impl`) used where a value is expected, or a value used as an object, or an object where objects may not stand (ADR-040) |
| [`E0065`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0065) | a signal of a store written off its owning runtime's core (ADR-035): a runtime message |
| [`E0066`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0066) | a `#[undra::migrate]` hook with a wrong target or shape (ADR-037; addition) |
| [`E0070`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0070) | a named instantiation of a generic data type that is declared twice or outside the crate of its template |
| [`E0071`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0071) | a method of a `#[undra::callback]` trait that is neither fire-and-forget nor `async` with a `Result`, or whose name starts with `__` (ADR-041) |
| [`E0072`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0072) | the instantiation list of a generic function or method (`generic(T = [Todo, Note])`) is empty, repeats a type, lists something that is not a named value type, names a type parameter the function does not have, or the function has several type parameters; a schema whose `generic` labels do not describe their definitions (ADR-058; addition) |
| [`E0073`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0073) | an `infinite` query that does not meet ADR-043's shape: no `item_key` or one that names no field of the rows, no or more than one `#[undra(cursor)]` parameter, a cursor that is not `Option<C>` or is in the key, a success type that is not `Page<T, C>`, rows that are not a record |
| [`E0074`](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#E0074) | the impl block of a generic object that is not for the type with its own type parameters, each exactly once, or a method of a generic object with type parameters of its own (ADR-058; addition) |

## Types and shapes

### `E0001` unsupported type in a public position

Raised by macros, schema validation, the `Encode`/`Decode` bounds.

unsupported type in a public position (lists the type and the allowed set); includes `i128`/`u128` (the help points at `Decimal`, `Uuid` or a `String` newtype), `DateTime<Local>` and `DateTime<FixedOffset>` ("convert to `Utc`; offsets do not cross"), a type of the `uuid`, `chrono`, `time`, `rust_decimal` or `bytes` crate that only that crate has (`DateTime<Utc>`, `OffsetDateTime`, `TimeDelta`, ..) spelled without the matching feature of `undra` (one error naming the feature), a `Lazy<T>` that is not a store field, or is inside a `Signal`, `Computed` or `DerivedList` (ADR-043), a `DerivedList` field without its row type (ADR-039), `Handle` (no schema type; an object crosses as `Arc<T>` or `&T`, ADR-040), `Arc<T>` of a built-in or an `Rc`, a `Result` whose error type is not a `#[undra::error]` enum, a `Ctx` parameter that is misplaced (on a method, not first, or `&mut`), and a type used as a value that cannot cross (an `Encode`/`Decode` bound that is not met: a struct without `#[undra::api]`)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Plain` cannot cross the boundary by value | a value crosses as a scalar, `String`, `Bytes`, `Vec`, `Option`, a map, `Duration`, `Timestamp`, `Uuid`, `Decimal`, or a type declared with `#[undra::api]` (records, enums) or `#[undra::error]`; an object (`#[undra::api] impl`) crosses by handle, never as a value | declare `Plain` with `#[undra::api]`, or return a record with the data the platform needs; a type of the `uuid`, `chrono`, `time`, `rust_decimal` or `bytes` crate crosses once you enable that feature of `undra` |
| `()` cannot be used as a field | `()` occupies zero bytes on the wire, so it is only legal as a return type or as a variant without fields; `Vec<()>`, `Option<()>` and maps of `()` defeat length validation | remove the value, or use `bool` if you need a marker |
| `DateTime<Local>` cannot cross the boundary | a `Timestamp` is an instant in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, in UTC; a date-time with a local time zone or a fixed offset has no one value every platform reads alike, and the offset itself would be lost | convert to `Utc` (`value.with_timezone(&Utc)`) and spell `DateTime<Utc>`; offsets do not cross |
| `DateTime<FixedOffset>` cannot cross the boundary | a `Timestamp` is an instant in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, in UTC; a date-time with a local time zone or a fixed offset has no one value every platform reads alike, and the offset itself would be lost | convert to `Utc` (`value.with_timezone(&Utc)`) and spell `DateTime<Utc>`; offsets do not cross |
| `DerivedList` needs the type of its rows | a derived list is a `Vec` of rows the platforms mirror, so the schema needs the row type, written as the one type argument | write `DerivedList<Row>` for `visible`, with the type the pipeline's `build()` produces |
| `&str` cannot cross the boundary | references have no wire representation; every value crosses by copy | use an owned `String` |

### `E0002` generic parameter, or a generic type spelled with its arguments

Raised by macros.

generic parameter on a `#[undra::api]` item that is not a template, on an error enum, object, store, function, method, constructor, port, callback, query or mutation (the text of each says what to write instead: `#[undra::api(generic)]` and a named instantiation for a data type; `generic(T = [Todo, Note])`, the list of types, for a function or method, ADR-058); a const parameter, a `where` clause or a default type parameter ("only type parameters are supported"); a generic type spelled with its arguments (`Page<Todo>`: declare `#[undra::api] pub type TodoPage = Page<Todo>;` and write `TodoPage`); the wrong number of type arguments for a template (ADR-042)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Page<Note>` has no name (in `first_page<Note>`) | the schema names every type, and an instantiated generic type is named by the alias that declares it; `Page<Note>` is reached here by putting a listed type in place of a type parameter, and no alias declares it | declare `#[undra::api] pub type NotePage = Page<Note>;` next to `Page` |
| generic parameter `T` on `newest` has no list of types | the schema describes concrete functions and the platforms call them by id: a generic function crosses once for each type it is declared for, and its callers are on the platforms, where the core cannot see them | list the types the platforms may use: `#[undra::api(generic(T = [Todo, Note]))]`; each becomes a function of its own, `newest<Todo>` and `newest<Note>` |
| generic parameter `T` on `pinned` has no list of types | the schema describes concrete functions and the platforms call them by id: a generic function crosses once for each type it is declared for, and its callers are on the platforms, where the core cannot see them | list the types the platforms may use: `#[undra(generic(T = [Todo, Note]))]` on the method; each becomes a method of its own, `pinned<Todo>` and `pinned<Note>` |
| generic parameter `T` on the constructor `create` | a constructor returns the object, and the object has no such parameter: the platforms could not say which `create` they mean | take a concrete type or an enum of the cases; make the object generic if the parameter belongs to it |
| generic parameter `T` on the store `Selection` | the schema describes concrete objects: a generic object crosses once per instantiation, each under a name of its own, which the platforms generate a class for | write `#[undra::store(generic)]`, mark its impl block `#[undra::api(store, generic)]` and declare each instantiation: `#[undra::api] pub type TodoSelection = Selection<Todo>;` |
| generic parameter `T` on the impl block of `Cache` | the schema describes concrete objects: a generic object crosses once per instantiation, each under a name of its own, which the platforms generate a class for | mark the block `#[undra::api(generic)]` (`#[undra::api(store, generic)]` for a store) and declare each instantiation: `#[undra::api] pub type TodoSelection = Selection<Todo>;` |

### `E0003` lifetime in a public signature

Raised by macros.

lifetime in a public signature

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lifetime `'static` in `&'static str` | everything crosses the boundary by value; a borrow cannot outlive the call that made it | use an owned type such as `String` or `Vec<T>` |
| lifetime `'a` on `WithLifetime` | everything crosses the boundary by value; a borrow cannot outlive the call that made it | remove the lifetime parameter and use owned types |
| lifetime `'a` in `&'a str` | everything crosses the boundary by value; a borrow cannot outlive the call that made it | use an owned type such as `String` or `Vec<T>` |
| lifetime `'a` on `Label` | everything crosses the boundary by value; a borrow cannot outlive the call that made it | remove the lifetime parameter and use owned types |

### `E0004` a trait object, `dyn` or `impl Trait` that is not a callback parameter, or a callback where one may not stand (ADR-041)

Raised by macros, schema validation (a bound the compiler checks).

trait object / `dyn` / `Box<dyn Fn>` / closure / function pointer / an `impl Trait` that is not a stream (declare a `#[undra::callback]` trait and take `Arc<dyn Trait>`, ADR-041); a callback (`Arc<dyn Trait>`) where one may not stand (anywhere but a parameter of a method, constructor or function, alone or in an `Option`: a return, a field, a signal, a port or query value), with the help of its position; `Arc<dyn Trait>` of a trait that is not a `#[undra::callback]` (the `CallbackInterface` bound, a branded message)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callback `Arc<dyn Listener>` cannot be a field of a record or enum (`Listener` is a callback interface) | a callback is an instance with a lifetime, not a value: it cannot be copied, compared, stored in a record or mirrored from a signal | keep an id or a record here, and take the callback as a parameter of the method that needs it |
| callback `Arc<dyn Listener>` cannot be used here (`Listener` is a callback interface) | a callback is an object the host implements and passes in for the core to call; the core never hands one out | return a plain value, or an object (`Arc<T>`) the host can call methods on |
| callback `Arc<dyn Listener>` cannot be used here (`Listener` is a callback interface) | a callback may be a parameter of a method, constructor or function, alone or in an `Option`; it cannot be nested in another type | take one `Arc<dyn Trait>` (or `Option<Arc<dyn Trait>>`) per parameter |
| closure type `Arc<dyn Fn(u32) + Send + Sync>` cannot cross the boundary | callbacks have no wire representation | declare a `#[undra::callback]` trait and take `Arc<dyn Trait>` |
| `dyn Platform` cannot be taken as a callback | only a trait declared with `#[undra::callback]` has a proxy the core can call and a generated protocol the host implements | add `#[undra::callback]` to the trait, or pass a record or an id |
| `dyn Plain` cannot be taken as a callback | only a trait declared with `#[undra::callback]` has a proxy the core can call and a generated protocol the host implements | add `#[undra::callback]` to the trait, or pass a record or an id |

### `E0005` `Result` / `Stream` outside return position

Raised by macros, schema validation.

`Result` or `Stream` outside return position; a `Result<impl Stream<Item = Result<T, E1>>, E2>` whose two error types differ (ADR-036)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Result<u32, String>` cannot be used as a field | `Result<T, E>` is how a method reports a typed error; it is only legal as the outermost type of a return | return the `Result` from the method and keep only plain values in fields, parameters and nested types |
| `Result<u32, String>` cannot be used as a parameter | `Result<T, E>` is how a method reports a typed error; it is only legal as the outermost type of a return | return the `Result` from the method and keep only plain values in fields, parameters and nested types |
| the items of the stream in `Result<impl Stream<Item = Result<u32, ItemError>>, OpenError>` fail with `ItemError` but its opening fails with `OpenError` | a stream method has one error type: the platforms throw it whether the stream fails to open or ends with an error part-way | use the same `#[undra::error]` enum for both (`OpenError`), or one enum with a variant for each case |
| `Result<u32, String>` cannot be nested inside another type | `Result<T, E>` is how a method reports a typed error; it is only legal as the outermost type of a return | return the `Result` from the method and keep only plain values in fields, parameters and nested types |
| `result<u8,named:Oops>` at record Todo, field outcome: Result is only allowed as the outermost type of a return | `Result<T, E>` is how a method reports a typed error, so it has no meaning inside a field, a parameter or another type | return the `Result` from the method and keep plain values in fields, parameters and nested types |

### `E0006` map key type not allowed

Raised by macros, schema validation, a bound the compiler checks.

map key type not allowed: `String`, integers, `bool`, `Uuid` and newtypes of those are keys; a float, a `Decimal`, a record, a collection, and a newtype of one of those are not (the macros assert `K: MapKey` at every `HashMap`/`BTreeMap` key position, ADR-042)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `f64` cannot be a map key | map keys must be `String`, an integer, `bool`, `Uuid` or a newtype of one of those: they compare and hash identically on every platform (floats, decimals, records and collections do not) | use one of those key types, a newtype of one (`struct UserId(pub Uuid);`), or a `Vec` of records with an explicit key field |
| `Decimal` cannot be a map key | map keys must be `String`, an integer, `bool`, `Uuid` or a newtype of one of those: they compare and hash identically on every platform (floats, decimals, records and collections do not) | use one of those key types, a newtype of one (`struct UserId(pub Uuid);`), or a `Vec` of records with an explicit key field |
| `undra::prelude::Decimal` cannot be a map key | map keys must be `String`, an integer, `bool`, `Uuid` or a newtype of one of those: they compare and hash identically on every platform (floats, decimals, records and collections do not) | use one of those key types, a newtype of one (`struct UserId(pub Uuid);`), or a `Vec` of records with an explicit key field |
| `Loose` cannot be a map key | map keys must be `String`, an integer, `bool`, `Uuid` or a newtype of one of those: they compare and hash identically on every platform (floats, decimals, records and collections do not) | use one of those key types, a newtype of one (`struct UserId(pub Uuid);`), or a `Vec` of records with an explicit key field |
| `f32` at record Scores, field by_weight is not a valid map key | map keys must compare and hash the same on every platform: `String`, an integer type, `bool`, `Uuid` and a newtype of one of those do, floats, decimals and composite keys do not | use one of those key types, or a `Vec` of records with an explicit key field |
| `decimal` at record Prices, field by_amount is not a valid map key | map keys must compare and hash the same on every platform: `String`, an integer type, `bool`, `Uuid` and a newtype of one of those do, floats, decimals and composite keys do not | use one of those key types, or a `Vec` of records with an explicit key field |

### `E0007` unsupported item shape or placement of an Undra attribute

Raised by macros.

unsupported item shape (a unit struct, a tuple struct of two or more fields or none (one field is a newtype), a record without fields, a type alias that does not name an instantiation of a `#[undra::api(generic)]` type, an empty enum, an impl item that is neither a method nor a constructor, a receiver that is not `&self`, a store that is not a struct with named fields, the reserved field name `__undra_cell`, `#[undra::port]` on an inherent impl, an Undra attribute on the wrong kind of item, `#[undra::api]` on a method, `#[undra::query]` or `#[undra::mutation]` inside an `impl` block or a port trait, a function whose signature uses `Self`, a second `#[undra::api]` impl block for one type). A second impl block is reported by `rustc` as "the name `_undra_error_E0007_<Type>_has_two_undra_api_impl_blocks_merge_them_into_one` is defined multiple times": merge the blocks. A query or mutation inside an impl block that is not `#[undra::api]` cannot be seen by its macro; `rustc` then reports "macro definition is not supported in `trait`s or `impl`s" and "cannot find macro `_undra_error_E0007_a_query_is_a_free_function_move_it_out_of_the_impl_block`", which is this code: move the function out of the block

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#[undra::api]` on `new`, which is an associated function: its signature uses `Self` | `Self` only exists inside an `impl` block, and `#[undra::api]` on a function exposes a free function; the functions of an object are exposed by putting the attribute on the `impl` block they are in | remove `#[undra::api]` from `new` and write `#[undra::api]` above the `impl` block (it exposes every `pub fn` in it) |
| `#[undra::query]` on the method `forecast` of a port trait | a port is a list of methods the platform implements; the attribute applies to a whole item (a type or a free function), never to a trait method | remove the attribute from `forecast`; a `#[undra::query]` is a free `async fn(ctx: &Ctx, ..)` that calls the port as `weather(ctx).forecast(..)`, so write it outside the trait |
| `#[undra::api]` on the method `now` of a port trait | a port is a list of methods the platform implements; the attribute applies to a whole item (a type or a free function), never to a trait method | remove the attribute from `now`; a function the core exposes that calls the port is a free `#[undra::api] fn(ctx: &Ctx, ..)` outside the trait, calling `weather(ctx).now(..)` |
| `#[undra::query]` on `admins`, which is inside an `impl` block: its signature uses `Self` | a query is a free function, and the macro generates a struct next to it, which an impl block cannot hold | move `admins` out of the impl block, to module level, and spell out the type instead of `Self` |
| `#[undra::store]` cannot be applied to an `enum` | `#[undra::store]` applies to a struct | move `#[undra::store]` onto a struct, or remove it |
| `#[undra::api]` on the type alias `Alias`, which does not name an instantiation | a type alias is not a schema type of its own; the only alias that is names an instantiation of a generic data type declared with `#[undra::api(generic)]`, so it can be given a name the platforms generate a type for | write `#[undra::api] pub type Alias = Page<Todo>;` for a template `Page`, or remove `#[undra::api]` and write the aliased type where it is used |

### `E0008` unknown or misplaced `#[undra(..)]` attribute or macro argument

Raised by macros.

unknown or misplaced `#[undra(..)]` attribute or macro argument (an unknown key, with the nearest name suggested, a value of the wrong kind or a value on a flag, `key` on a signal that is not a `Signal<Vec<T>>` or a `DerivedList<T>` (a keyed `Computed` is pointed at `DerivedList<T>`), a `DerivedList<T>` without `key` (ADR-039), `key` naming no field of the list's items (for a generic store: of the row type of one instantiation, at its alias), `generic` on a type, an impl block or a store that has no type parameter, `generic(..)` with a list on a struct, an enum or an impl block (a list instantiates a function; a type is instantiated by an alias, ADR-058), `generic` alone on a function, a malformed list, `#[cfg]` on a public item, an invalid `crate = ".."` path); a `cfg_attr` whose attributes are all documentation or lint levels is accepted

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#[undra(key = "idd")]` on `typo` names no field of `Row` | `key` names the field of the list's items that identifies them, and `Row` has the fields `id`, `title` | write the name of one of those fields as the key |
| `#[undra(key = "n")]` on `not_a_record` names no field of `u32` | `key` names the field of the list's items that identifies them, and `u32` has no fields (only a record declared with `#[undra::api]` has any) | write the name of one of those fields as the key |
| `#[undra(key = "not a name")]` on `not_a_name` names no field of `Tagged` | `key` names the field of the list's items that identifies them, and `Tagged` has the fields `type`, `id` | write the name of one of those fields as the key |
| unknown option `defualt` in `#[undra(..)]` | the options are `crate = "path"` (items), `default` (record fields), `key = "field"` and `no_coalesce` (store signal fields), `coalesce` (fire-and-forget methods of a callback interface) and `generic(T = [..])` (methods with a type parameter) | did you mean `default`? Otherwise remove `defualt` |
| unknown option `frobnicate` in `#[undra(..)]` | the options are `crate = "path"` (items), `default` (record fields), `key = "field"` and `no_coalesce` (store signal fields), `coalesce` (fire-and-forget methods of a callback interface) and `generic(T = [..])` (methods with a type parameter) | remove `frobnicate`, or use one of: `crate`, `default`, `key`, `no_coalesce`, `coalesce`, `generic` |
| `#[undra(key)]` is not valid on a record or variant field | `key = "field"` turns a store's `Signal<Vec<T>>` into a keyed list that ships patches | move it to a `Signal<Vec<T>>` field of a `#[undra::store]` struct, or remove it |

## Errors and stores

### `E0010` invalid `#[undra::error]` variant

Raised by macros, schema validation.

`#[undra::error]` variant without `#[error(..)]`, a message with an implicit `{}` (write `{0}` or `{name}`), `#[error]`, `#[from]` or `#[source]` on a plain `#[undra::api]` enum

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| variant `NotFound` has no `#[error(..)]` message | every variant of a `#[undra::error]` enum needs a message, because the platforms show it to users and logs | add `#[error("what went wrong")]`, or `#[error(transparent)]` to forward to the inner error |
| invalid message for variant `Missing`: `{1}` refers to field 1, but the variant has 1 | the message is a template over the variant's fields | use `{0}`, `{1}`, .. for tuple fields and `{name}` for named fields |
| `#[error(transparent)]` on variant `Both` needs exactly one field, found 2 | `transparent` forwards `Display` and `source()` to the variant's only field | give the variant a single field holding the inner error |
| `#[error]` on the variant `A` belongs to `#[undra::error]`, not `#[undra::api]` | `#[error(..)]`, `#[from]` and `#[source]` are the helper attributes of error enums; a plain `#[undra::api]` enum has no messages, `Display` or `From` impls | change the enum's attribute to `#[undra::error]`, or remove the helper attribute |
| `#[from]` on the field `0` belongs to `#[undra::error]`, not `#[undra::api]` | `#[error(..)]`, `#[from]` and `#[source]` are the helper attributes of error enums; a plain `#[undra::api]` enum has no messages, `Display` or `From` impls | change the enum's attribute to `#[undra::error]`, or remove the helper attribute |
| variant `Unmessaged` has no `#[error(..)]` message | every variant of a `#[undra::error]` enum needs a message, because the platforms show it to users and logs | add `#[error("what went wrong")]`, or `#[error(transparent)]` to forward to the inner error |

### `E0011` store and `#[undra::api(store)]` impl block disagree

Raised by macros, schema validation.

`#[undra::store]` and its `#[undra::api(store)]` impl block disagree, including a store with no impl block and a `#[undra::api(store)]` block without a constructor (a type takes one block; a constructor in another block is not seen); a store without a constructor in the schema; for a generic store (ADR-058) the impl block below its struct in the same module: a block that is not below a `#[undra::store(generic)]` struct is reported by `rustc` as "cannot find macro `_undra_error_E0011_<Type>_is_not_a_generic_store_declared_above_this_impl_block_in_the_same_module`", a `#[undra::store(generic)]` whose block is `#[undra::api(generic)]` without `store` by a const assertion at the alias, and a `#[undra::store(generic)]` with no generic block at all by "cannot find macro `Selection` in this scope ... `Selection` is in scope, but it is a struct, not a macro": write the block

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| store `Counter` has no constructor in this `#[undra::api(store)]` block | the platforms create a store by calling one of its constructors, and a type takes one `#[undra::api]` impl block, so a constructor in another block is not seen | add `pub fn new(ctx: Ctx) -> Self` to this block; if `Counter` has a second `#[undra::api]` block (where the constructor is), move this block's methods into that one |
| `Selection` is a `#[undra::store(generic)]` but its impl block is not marked as a store | the impl block of a store must say so, so its constructors can attach the store's signals and its struct literals get the hidden cell field | write `#[undra::api(store, generic)]` on the impl block |
| `Todos` is a `#[undra::store]` but its `#[undra::api]` impl block is not marked as a store | the impl block of a store must say so, so its constructors can attach the store's signals and its struct literals get the hidden cell field | write `#[undra::api(store)]` on the impl block |
| `Plain` is implemented with `#[undra::api(store)]` but the struct has no `#[undra::store]` | the `store` marker wires the constructors to the struct's signals, which only `#[undra::store]` sets up | add `#[undra::store]` to `struct Plain`, or remove `store` from the impl attribute |
| store `Todos` has no `#[undra::api(store)]` impl block | the constructors of the impl block create the store and wire its signals to the platforms; without the block the store can never be instantiated | add an `impl Todos` block marked `#[undra::api(store)]` with a constructor such as `pub fn new(ctx: Ctx) -> Self` |
| store `Counter` has no constructor | the platforms create a store by calling one of its constructors; without one it can never be instantiated | add `pub fn new(ctx: Ctx) -> Self` to its `#[undra::api(store)]` impl block |

### `E0012` trait object in a record field

Raised by macros.

trait object in a record field (the blueprint example)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Vec<Box<dyn Any>>` cannot cross the boundary | trait objects have no wire representation | make `items` a concrete `#[undra::api]` type, or an enum listing the cases you need |

### `E0013` store cannot be restored automatically

Raised by macros.

store cannot be restored automatically: it has a `Computed` field, or a field that is neither a signal, a `Ctx`, a `WeakCtx` nor `Default`, and no `#[undra::store(restore = "..")]` hook

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| store `Todos` cannot be restored automatically: `count` is computed | restoring a snapshot decodes the plain signals and rebuilds the store, but only your code knows how to derive computed signals from them | add `#[undra::store(restore = "Self::rebuild")]` with `fn rebuild(ctx: Ctx, <one Signal<T> per plain signal, in order>) -> Self`, the same code `new` uses to build the store |
| store `Sync` cannot be restored automatically: its field of type `Config` has no `Default` | restoring a snapshot rebuilds the store from its plain signals and fills every other field with `Default::default()` (a `Ctx` is cloned from the argument, a `WeakCtx` downgraded from it) | implement `Default` for the type, or add `#[undra::store(restore = "Self::rebuild")]` with `fn rebuild(ctx: Ctx, <one Signal<T> per plain signal, in order>) -> Self`, the same code `new` uses to build the store |

## Methods

### `E0020` `&mut self` receiver

Raised by macros.

`&mut self` receiver

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `&mut self` receiver on method `clear` | objects are shared as `Arc<Type>` across calls and threads, so methods only ever get `&self` | take `&self` and mutate through signals (`Signal<T>`), a `Mutex` or another form of interior mutability |
| `&mut self` receiver on method `increment` | objects are shared as `Arc<Type>` across calls and threads, so methods only ever get `&self` | take `&self` and mutate through signals (`Signal<T>`), a `Mutex` or another form of interior mutability |

### `E0021` `self` by value

Raised by macros.

`self` by value

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `self` by value on method `finish` | an object is shared across calls; a method cannot consume it | take `&self` and clone whatever you need to keep |

### `E0022` non-`Send` future in an async method: `rustc`'s own error, pointed at the method by an assertion named after this code

Raised by rustc, named by a macro.

non-`Send` future in an async method or query: `rustc`'s own "future cannot be sent between threads safely", pointed at the method by an assertion the macros emit; the last note names the assertion, `_undra_error_E0022_the_future_of_an_async_method_must_be_Send`. Do not hold a non-`Send` value (an `Rc`, a `RefCell` borrow, a `MutexGuard`) across an `.await`

The compiler reports this one itself, so it carries no Undra code. It is pointed at the method, and the last note names the assertion the macro emitted, `_undra_error_E0022_the_future_of_an_async_method_must_be_Send`: the code to look up.

text

```
error: future cannot be sent between threads safely
  --> src/lib.rs:15:18
   |
15 |     pub async fn run(&self) -> u32 {
   |                  ^^^ future created by async block is not `Send`
   |
   = help: within `{async block@src/lib.rs:9:1: 9:10}`, the trait `Send` is not implemented for `Rc<u32>`
note: future is not `Send` as this value is used across an await
  --> src/lib.rs:17:32
   |
16 |         let local = Rc::new(1_u32);
   |             ----- has type `Rc<u32>` which is not `Send`
17 |         std::future::ready(()).await;
   |                                ^^^^^ await occurs here, with `local` maybe used later
note: required by a bound in `_undra_error_E0022_the_future_of_an_async_method_must_be_Send`
  --> src/lib.rs:9:1
   |
 9 | #[k::api]
   | ^^^^^^^^^ required by this bound in `_undra_error_E0022_the_future_of_an_async_method_must_be_Send`
   = note: this error originates in the attribute macro `k::api` (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)
```

## Ports

### `E0030` port method with a non-wire parameter

Raised by macros.

port method with a non-wire parameter

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| parameter `listener` of port method `call` is not a wire type | callback `Arc<dyn Listener>` cannot be a parameter of a port (`Listener` is a callback interface) (a port is implemented once, by the platform, for the whole process; a callback instance in its arguments would need a wrapper type the port implementation does not have) | pass a record or an id through the port |
| parameter `url` of port method `request` is not a wire type | `&str` cannot cross the boundary (references have no wire representation; every value crosses by copy) | use an owned `String` |
| parameter `on_progress` of port method `request` is not a wire type | trait object `dyn Fn(u8)` cannot cross the boundary (trait objects have no wire representation and no equivalent in Swift, Kotlin or TypeScript) | use a concrete `#[undra::api]` type or an enum listing the cases you need; to call into the platform, declare a `#[undra::callback]` trait and take `Arc<dyn Trait>` as a parameter |
| parameter `child` of port method `open` is not a wire type | object `Arc<Child>` cannot be a parameter of a port (a port implementation on the platform would receive a reference it has no wrapper type for) | pass a record or an id through the port (the object here is `Child`) |

### `E0031` event port method that is not a plain `fn(..)` returning `()`

Raised by macros, schema validation.

event port method with a return type, or that is `async`

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| event port method `changed` returns a value | events are fire-and-forget notifications from the host; there is no reply to carry a value | remove the return type, or drop `event` from `#[undra::port(event)]` to make it a request/reply port |
| event port method `resumed` is `async` | events are fire-and-forget notifications from the host; nothing waits for them | make it a plain `fn` returning `()` |
| event port `Connectivity` method `changed` returns a value or is `async` | events are fire-and-forget notifications from the host; nothing waits for them, so there is no reply to carry a value | make the method a plain `fn` returning `()`, or make the port a request/reply port |

### `E0032` invalid port trait shape

Raised by macros.

invalid port trait shape (an `async` method on a `sync` port, a parameter that is not a plain name, an associated type or const, no `&self` receiver)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#[undra::port(sync)]` port has the `async` method `now_ms` | `sync` promises that every method answers immediately, so the core can call it without yielding | remove `async`, or remove `sync` from the attribute |
| port trait `Kv` has an associated item that is not a method | a port is a list of methods the platform implements; associated types and constants have no wire representation | remove it, or move it to a separate trait |

### `E0033` the error type of a port method has no `From<PortError>`

Raised by macros (a bound the compiler checks).

the error type of a `Result` port method has no `From<PortError>` (an unavailable port cannot be reported)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the error type `StoreError` of a method of the `Store` port cannot represent a port that is unavailable | a port nobody registered, a cancelled call and a reply that does not decode are ordinary outcomes (SPEC 6.3), and a method that returns `Result<T, E>` reports them as its error instead of panicking; that needs `From<PortError>` for the error type | implement `From<undra::runtime::PortError>` for `StoreError`, mapping it to a variant such as `Unavailable`, or to the `Display` text of the `PortError` |

## Queries and mutations

### `E0040` query without `key`, mutation with `stale`, or another invalid query argument

Raised by macros.

query without `key` / mutation with `stale` / a query argument of the wrong kind, an `interval` below one second (use a stream for real-time data), `refetch_pages` or `persist_pages` that is not a whole number of at least 1, polling or paging options on a mutation

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interval = "500ms"` is below one second | a poll fetches the whole result again each time, so a query polled more than once a second is really a stream: use a stream for real-time data | write `interval = "1s"` or more, or deliver the changes with a `#[undra::port]` event or a stream |
| `interval = "0s"` is below one second | a poll fetches the whole result again each time, so a query polled more than once a second is really a stream: use a stream for real-time data | write `interval = "1s"` or more, or deliver the changes with a `#[undra::port]` event or a stream |
| invalid `interval` duration: `soon` does not start with a whole number | `interval` is how long after a fetch ends the next one starts | write a whole number and a unit, for example `interval = "30s"` |
| mutation `add` has `interval` | polling and paging apply to cached reads; a mutation writes and caches nothing | remove `interval`; put it on the query the mutation invalidates |
| query `todos` has no `key` | the cache is addressed by key: two calls share a cached result only if their keys are equal | add `key = "todos"`, with `{param}` placeholders for the parameters that distinguish results |
| mutation `add_todo` has `stale` | `stale` is how long a cached *read* stays fresh; a mutation writes and caches nothing | remove `stale`; put it on the query the mutation invalidates |

### `E0041` query or mutation function with an invalid signature

Raised by macros.

query or mutation function with an invalid signature (not `async`, no `ctx: &Ctx` first parameter, not returning `Result<T, E>`, a stream result, `self`)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sync_query` must be `async` | `#[undra::query]` functions fetch or write through ports, which are asynchronous | write `async fn` |
| `no_ctx` must take `ctx: &Ctx` as its first parameter | the runtime hands every query and mutation a context to reach ports and other queries | add `ctx: &Ctx` (or `ctx: Ctx`) before the other parameters |
| `plain` must return `Result<T, E>` | the cache stores the success value and the error separately, and the platforms show both | return `Result<T, E>` where `E` is a `#[undra::error]` enum |

### `E0042` query whose success value is `()` or an `Option`

Raised by macros.

query whose success value is `()` or an `Option` (a query caches a value; use a mutation for effects)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| query `ping` returns `()` | a query caches the value it returns; a query with nothing to return has nothing to cache | use `#[undra::mutation]` for a call that only has effects, or return the data the platform needs |
| query `find` returns an `Option` | the handle's `data` signal is already optional (no result yet), so an optional result would be ambiguous: `None` could mean "not loaded" or "loaded, absent" | return a record or a list (an empty `Vec` says "nothing"), or an enum naming the cases |

## Names in the generators

### `E0050` duplicate type name, id or variant index

Raised by schema validation.

duplicate type name, a type named like something the generated code depends on, two items with one id, two variants with one index

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| duplicate type name `Todo` (declared as record and again as enum) | type names must be unique within a core: a type is identified to the platforms by its name (its id is a hash of it), so two declarations cannot share one | rename one of the two `Todo` declarations, or remove the duplicate |
| duplicate type name `Storage` at the port `Storage` (the name is already used by a record) | names and ids identify a type, a method or a variant to the platforms and in the generated code, so each must be unique within a core | rename one of the two, or remove the duplicate |
| record `Signal` has a name the generated code depends on | the generated bindings use a type called `Signal` (a standard type of Swift, Kotlin or TypeScript, or one of the Undra runtime's), so a type of the schema with the same name would shadow it | rename it, for example `MySignal` |
| duplicate type id `0x00000007` at the schema (`Alpha` and `Beta` hash to the same id) | names and ids identify a type, a method or a variant to the platforms and in the generated code, so each must be unique within a core | rename one of the two items: ids are hashes of the names, so a different name gives a different id |
| duplicate variant index `1` at enum Status | names and ids identify a type, a method or a variant to the platforms and in the generated code, so each must be unique within a core | give every variant of the enum an index of its own |
| duplicate type name `Todo` (declared as record and again as record) | type names must be unique within a core: a type is identified to the platforms by its name (its id is a hash of it), so two declarations cannot share one | rename one of the two `Todo` declarations, or remove the duplicate |

### `E0051` a name that collides after case conversion or is not an identifier

Raised by schema validation.

a name that collides after case conversion (`a_b` and `aB`), shadows a member of the runtime base classes, or is not an identifier in a target language; in the iOS 15 / 16 Swift mode also a store member named `objectWillChange` (§10.1, ADR-045)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| at record Todo, `due_date`, `dueDate` all become `dueDate` | field names are converted to camelCase, so names that differ only in case or underscores end up equal | rename one of them so that they stay distinct after conversion |
| at object Thing, `close` is a name the generated code already uses | the runtime base class or the generated code already declares a member with that name | rename it so that it does not meet that name |
| at record Todo, `1st` is not a name the generated code can use | every name of the schema becomes an identifier in Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript: ASCII letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit | rename it to letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter |
| at object Counter, `object_will_change` becomes `objectWillChange`, a name the generated code already uses | with the iOS 15 / 16 store shape (`swift_observation = "observable-object"`, the default for a deployment target below iOS 17) a store is a Combine `ObservableObject`, which declares that member itself | rename it so that it does not meet that name |
| at the schema, `newest<Todo>`, `newest_todo` all become `newestTodo` | id constants are named in camelCase in Swift and TypeScript, and the id of an instantiation of a generic function names the function and the type, so names that differ only in case or underscores end up equal | rename one of them so that they stay distinct after conversion |
| at the schema, `newest<Todo>`, `newest_todo` all become `NEWEST_TODO` | id constants are named UPPER_SNAKE_CASE in Kotlin, and the id of an instantiation of a generic function names the function and the type, so names that differ only in case or underscores end up equal | rename one of them so that they stay distinct after conversion |

### `E0052` an item named like a standard library item, with another id

Raised by schema validation.

a record, enum, error, object or port named like a standard library item (section 8) but with another id: the runtimes implement the standard items under those names and ids

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| record `HttpRequest` has the name of an Undra standard library item but the id 0x00000007 instead of 0xbbbc6e52 | every platform runtime implements the standard ports and types under those names and ids, and generated code refers to them instead of declaring them, so a different item cannot share the name | rename it, for example `MyHttpRequest`, or use the standard one from `undra-ports` |

## Type identity and the schema

### `E0060` a spelling that looks like a built-in Undra type is another type

Raised by macros (a check the compiler runs).

a spelling that looks like a built-in Undra type (`Bytes`, `Uuid`, `String`, `Vec`, ..) is a different type; reported at the field or parameter by the same-type assertion the macros emit; for a wire leaf (`Uuid`, `Timestamp`, `Duration`, `Bytes`, `Decimal`) by the membership assertion `Spelled: WireLeaf<kind>`, whose message names the leaves and the features (`uuid`, `chrono`, `time`, `rust_decimal`, `bytes`) that add the types of other crates (ADR-042)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bytes` is spelled like a built-in Undra type, but it is not one | the schema records this position as a wire leaf (`Uuid`, `Timestamp`, `Duration`, `Bytes` or `Decimal`), so the platforms would read the bytes of that leaf where the generated code writes `Bytes` | rename your type, import the built-in one, or, for a type of the `uuid`, `chrono`, `time`, `rust_decimal` or `bytes` crate, enable that feature of `undra` |
| `Uuid` is spelled like a built-in Undra type, but it is not one | the schema records this position as a wire leaf (`Uuid`, `Timestamp`, `Duration`, `Bytes` or `Decimal`), so the platforms would read the bytes of that leaf where the generated code writes `Uuid` | rename your type, import the built-in one, or, for a type of the `uuid`, `chrono`, `time`, `rust_decimal` or `bytes` crate, enable that feature of `undra` |
| `Timestamp` is spelled like a built-in Undra type, but it is not one | the schema records this position as a wire leaf (`Uuid`, `Timestamp`, `Duration`, `Bytes` or `Decimal`), so the platforms would read the bytes of that leaf where the generated code writes `Timestamp` | rename your type, import the built-in one, or, for a type of the `uuid`, `chrono`, `time`, `rust_decimal` or `bytes` crate, enable that feature of `undra` |
| `Decimal` is spelled like a built-in Undra type, but it is not one | the schema records this position as a wire leaf (`Uuid`, `Timestamp`, `Duration`, `Bytes` or `Decimal`), so the platforms would read the bytes of that leaf where the generated code writes `Decimal` | rename your type, import the built-in one, or, for a type of the `uuid`, `chrono`, `time`, `rust_decimal` or `bytes` crate, enable that feature of `undra` |

### `E0061` the name written is not the declared name of the type, or the type is not declared with `#[undra::api]`

Raised by macros (a check the compiler runs).

the schema records a name that the type written there does not have: an alias of an Undra type (`type Todo = Item`), a renamed import (`use m::Item as Todo`), or a name that is not a type declared with `#[undra::api]` at all (a plain struct, `type Id = u64`); reported by a const assertion on `UNDRA_TYPE_ID`

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Plain` is not a type declared with `#[undra::api]` | Undra describes a type to the platforms by the name it is written with, so the name must be a record or enum declared with `#[undra::api]` or an error declared with `#[undra::error]`; anything else, such as a plain struct or an alias (`type Id = u64`), has no definition the platforms could generate | add `#[undra::api]` to `Plain`, or, if it is an alias, write the type it stands for where it is used |
| `Id` is not a type declared with `#[undra::api]` | Undra describes a type to the platforms by the name it is written with, so the name must be a record or enum declared with `#[undra::api]` or an error declared with `#[undra::error]`; anything else, such as a plain struct or an alias (`type Id = u64`), has no definition the platforms could generate | add `#[undra::api]` to `Id`, or, if it is an alias, write the type it stands for where it is used |
| `Kid` here is an alias or a renamed import of an object that is declared under another name | Undra describes an object to the platforms by the name it is written with, while the handle the core issues is of the type that name resolves to; with `type Kid = Other` or `use path::Other as Kid` the platforms would wrap it as `Kid` | write the object under the name it is declared with (`Other` in the examples above) |
| `LostPage` here is an alias or a renamed import of an Undra type that is declared under another name | Undra describes a type to the platforms by the name it is written with, while the generated code encodes the type that name resolves to; with `type LostPage = Other` or `use path::Other as LostPage` the platforms would be told `LostPage` and receive the layout of `Other` | write the type under the name it is declared with (`Other` in the examples above), or declare a separate `#[undra::api] struct LostPage` if you mean a distinct type |
| `Todo` here is an alias or a renamed import of an Undra type that is declared under another name | Undra describes a type to the platforms by the name it is written with, while the generated code encodes the type that name resolves to; with `type Todo = Other` or `use path::Other as Todo` the platforms would be told `Todo` and receive the layout of `Other` | write the type under the name it is declared with (`Other` in the examples above), or declare a separate `#[undra::api] struct Todo` if you mean a distinct type |
| `Entry` here is an alias or a renamed import of an Undra type that is declared under another name | Undra describes a type to the platforms by the name it is written with, while the generated code encodes the type that name resolves to; with `type Entry = Other` or `use path::Other as Entry` the platforms would be told `Entry` and receive the layout of `Other` | write the type under the name it is declared with (`Other` in the examples above), or declare a separate `#[undra::api] struct Entry` if you mean a distinct type |

### `E0062` a port call could not be answered and its method has no error channel: a runtime message

Raised by runtime (the generated port proxy).

a port call that cannot be answered and has no error channel: no adapter registered, a cancelled call, a reply that does not decode. A method without an error channel panics with this message (the runtime contains the panic at the dispatch boundary; on wasm it traps the core); a method returning `Result` reports it as its error type, and `HttpError::Network` / `FsError::Io` carry the code and the link

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the `Rng` port has no adapter registered (method `fill`) | this method has no error channel, so an unavailable port cannot be reported and the call panics; the runtime contains the panic, but on the web it traps the core | register an adapter (`core.registerPort(..)` in TypeScript, Kotlin and Swift, `undra_port_register` in C), bind a Rust implementation (`undra::ports::fakes` in tests), or give the method a `Result<T, E>` return type so it can report the outage |

### `E0063` nested `Option<Option<T>>`

Raised by macros.

`Option<Option<T>>` in a public position

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nested option `Option<Option<u8>>` cannot cross the boundary | Kotlin and TypeScript cannot express nested optionality: `Some(None)` and `None` would both arrive as `null` | wrap the inner option in a record or an enum that names the two cases |
| nested option `Option<Option<i32>>` cannot cross the boundary | Kotlin and TypeScript cannot express nested optionality: `Some(None)` and `None` would both arrive as `null` | wrap the inner option in a record or an enum that names the two cases |
| nested option `Option<Box<Option<u8>>>` cannot cross the boundary | Kotlin and TypeScript cannot express nested optionality: `Some(None)` and `None` would both arrive as `null` | wrap the inner option in a record or an enum that names the two cases |

### `E0064` an object (`#[undra::api] impl`) used where a value is expected, or a value used as an object, or an object where objects may not stand (ADR-040)

Raised by macros (a check the compiler runs), schema validation.

an object (`#[undra::api] impl`) used as a value (a field, a parameter or a return written `Mailbox`): it crosses as `Arc<Mailbox>` or `&Mailbox`; a record, enum or error written as an object (`Arc<Todo>`, `&Todo`: records cross by value); an object where objects may not stand (a record or variant field, a signal, a map key or value, a stream item, a port, callback, query or mutation value, or nested deeper than `Option` or `Vec`), with the reason and the way out of its position (ADR-040)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Calculator` is an object and cannot be used as a value | an object lives in the core and crosses the boundary as a handle; its contents have no wire representation, so it cannot be a field, a variant field, a signal value, a map entry or a query value | return it as `Arc<Calculator>`, take it as `&Calculator` or `Arc<Calculator>` (a method, constructor or function parameter or return), or use a record with the data the platform needs |
| `NotAnObject` is not an object | an object is a type with an `#[undra::api] impl` block: the macro generates what lets the core hand it to the platforms as a handle, and without one there is nothing to hand out | add `#[undra::api]` to an `impl NotAnObject { .. }` block, or use a record (`#[undra::api] struct`) if it is plain data |
| object `Arc<Child>` cannot be a field of a record or enum | a record or enum field holds a value: it is copied, compared, hashed and `Codable`, and none of that can carry a reference to an object | keep the data the platform needs in the field (an id, a record), and put the child object behind a method of the parent (the object here is `Child`) |
| object `Arc<Child>` cannot be used here | an object can only stand alone, or inside `Option` or `Vec`, as a method or function parameter or return | use `Arc<T>`, `Option<Arc<T>>` or `Vec<Arc<T>>` (a parameter may also be `&T` or `Option<&T>`) (the object here is `Child`) |
| `&Child` cannot be an element of a list | a list owns its elements, and a borrow of an object cannot outlive the call that made it | write the list as `Vec<Arc<Child>>` |
| object `Arc<Child>` cannot be the result of a query or mutation | query and mutation values are cached, compared and persisted, so they must be values | use a record or an id, and return the object from a method that calls the query (the object here is `Child`) |

### `E0065` a signal of a store written off its owning runtime's core (ADR-035): a runtime message

Raised by runtime (the write check of `undra-signals`).

a signal of a store was written from a thread that does not hold the owning runtime's core lock: a blocking-pool worker, a host or embedder thread, a thread inside no runtime, or another runtime's core. A panic with this message, in every build; `Signal::try_set` / `try_update` return it as `WriteError::OffCore` (ADR-035)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a signal of a store owned by runtime 5 was written from a thread that does not hold its core lock | signal writes belong on the core: the runtime delivers each change-set to its host in commit order under its core lock, so a write from any other thread (a blocking-pool worker, a host or embedder thread, another runtime's core) would be delivered unordered, to the wrong host, or not at all | return the value to the task or call that awaits it (`ctx.spawn`, a dispatched call, the result of `spawn_blocking`), or wrap the write in `ctx.with_core(\|\| ..)` on a host thread; `Signal::try_set` reports this as a `WriteError` instead of panicking |

### `E0066` a `#[undra::migrate]` hook with a wrong target or shape (ADR-037; addition)

Raised by macros, runtime (start-up check of the registered hooks).

a `#[undra::migrate]` hook with a wrong target or shape (ADR-037): no target or more than one, `signal` without `store`, a `from` that is not a 64-bit hex fingerprint, a function that is not a plain non-generic `fn` taking the target's old value (`&DynValue`, `Option<&DynValue>` or `&DynRecord`) and returning `Result<_, MigrateError>`, a `ty = "X"` hook that does not return the `#[undra::api]` type `X` (a const assertion the compiler runs); a store, signal or mutation the core does not have, or a signal hook returning another type than the signal's, is logged at ERROR with this code when a runtime starts (the macro cannot see those items)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#[undra::migrate]` needs a target | a migration hook converts persisted data of one record or enum, one signal of one store, or one mutation's queued input to this build's types; the runtime finds it by that target and calls it with the old value in a fixed shape | name exactly one target: `ty = "Todo"`, `store = "Profile", signal = "age"` or `mutation = "add_todo"` |
| `#[undra::migrate]` names more than one target | a migration hook converts persisted data of one record or enum, one signal of one store, or one mutation's queued input to this build's types; the runtime finds it by that target and calls it with the old value in a fixed shape | name exactly one target: `ty = "Todo"`, `store = "Profile", signal = "age"` or `mutation = "add_todo"` |
| `signal = ".."` needs `store = ".."` | a migration hook converts persisted data of one record or enum, one signal of one store, or one mutation's queued input to this build's types; the runtime finds it by that target and calls it with the old value in a fixed shape | name the store the signal belongs to: `store = "Profile", signal = "age"` |
| the migration hook `wrong_parameter` must take one parameter, `old: Option<&DynValue>` | a migration hook converts persisted data of one record or enum, one signal of one store, or one mutation's queued input to this build's types; the runtime finds it by that target and calls it with the old value in a fixed shape | write `fn wrong_parameter(old: Option<&DynValue>) -> Result<T, MigrateError>`, where `T` is the signal's value type (`old` is `None` when the snapshot lacks the signal): a plain, non-generic, non-async function |
| the migration hook `wrong_return` must return `Result<DynRecord, MigrateError>` | a migration hook converts persisted data of one record or enum, one signal of one store, or one mutation's queued input to this build's types; the runtime finds it by that target and calls it with the old value in a fixed shape | write `fn wrong_return(old: &DynRecord) -> Result<DynRecord, MigrateError>`: a plain, non-generic, non-async function |
| `from = "not-hex"` is not a fingerprint | a migration hook converts persisted data of one record or enum, one signal of one store, or one mutation's queued input to this build's types; the runtime finds it by that target and calls it with the old value in a fixed shape | write the 64-bit fingerprint of the old type in hex, as the runtime's log or `undra.types.<fingerprint>` key shows it: `from = "0x0123456789abcdef"`, or leave `from` out to take every old version |

### `E0070` a named instantiation of a generic data type that is declared twice or outside the crate of its template

Raised by macros (a check the compiler runs).

a named instantiation of a generic data type, object or store (`type TodoPage = Page<Todo>`, `type TodoSelection = Selection<Todo>`) declared twice, or outside the crate of its template (ADR-042, ADR-058; for an object or a store a module-level constant `_undra_error_E0070_this_instantiation_of_Selection_Todo_is_declared_twice_keep_one_alias_per_instantiation` makes a second alias in the same module the first error `rustc` reports): the inherent impl of the instantiation carries a constant named after the rule (`_undra_error_E0070_this_instantiation_of_Page_is_declared_twice_keep_one_alias_per_instantiation`), so a second alias of one instantiation is reported by `rustc` as that constant defined twice; an alias in another crate than its template's is reported by the macro itself, naming both crates

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TodoPage` instantiates `Page`, which is declared in the crate `model`, not in `app` | an instantiation adds an inherent impl to the template's type, which only the crate that declares the template may do, and a second crate naming the same instantiation would register it twice | declare the alias next to the template, in `model`, and use it from here; or declare a concrete `#[undra::api]` struct or enum in this crate |

### `E0071` a method of a `#[undra::callback]` trait that is neither fire-and-forget nor `async` with a `Result`, or whose name starts with `__` (ADR-041)

Raised by macros, schema validation.

a method of a `#[undra::callback]` trait that returns a value synchronously, is `async` without a `Result`, whose name starts with `__` (reserved for `__release` and `__cancel`), or an `async` method marked `#[undra(coalesce)]` (ADR-041): the host runs a callback outside the core's thread and lock, so the core can never wait for it, and a host can always fail or be gone; a method reports (`fn m(&self, ..)`) or is `async` and returns `Result<T, E>`

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callback method `token` returns a value synchronously | the host runs a callback outside the core's thread and lock, so the core can never wait for it synchronously, and a host implementation can always fail or be gone | make it `async` and return `Result<T, E>`, or make it a plain `fn` that returns nothing |
| callback method `ask` is `async` and returns nothing | the host runs a callback outside the core's thread and lock, so the core can never wait for it synchronously, and a host implementation can always fail or be gone | return `Result<T, E>` (an `#[undra::error]` enum that implements `From<PortError>`), or remove `async` to make it a fire-and-forget report |
| callback method `count` is `async` but does not return a `Result` | the host runs a callback outside the core's thread and lock, so the core can never wait for it synchronously, and a host implementation can always fail or be gone | return `Result<T, E>` so the method can report that the host failed or is gone |
| `#[undra(coalesce)]` on the `async` callback method `confirm` | `coalesce` drops the older of two pending calls, and an `async` method's caller is waiting for each answer | remove `#[undra(coalesce)]`, or make the method a plain `fn` that reports progress |
| callback method `__release` has a reserved name | names that start with `__` belong to the protocol (`__release` gives an instance back, `__cancel` cancels a call): a method of that name would be mistaken for one | rename the method |
| method `token` of the callback interface `Provider` returns a value synchronously: make it `async` and return a `Result<T, E>` | the host runs a callback outside the core's thread and lock, so the core can never wait for it synchronously, and a host implementation can always fail or be gone: a method either reports (fire-and-forget, returning nothing) or is `async` and returns a `Result` | make a reporting method return `()`, or make a method that answers `async` and return `Result<T, E>`; do not start a name with `__` |

### `E0072` the instantiation list of a generic function or method (`generic(T = [Todo, Note])`) is empty, repeats a type, lists something that is not a named value type, names a type parameter the function does not have, or the function has several type parameters; a schema whose `generic` labels do not describe their definitions (ADR-058; addition)

Raised by macros, schema validation.

the instantiation list of a generic function or method (ADR-058): a list for a parameter the function does not have, an empty list, a type listed twice, a type that is not a named value type (`Vec<Todo>`, a scalar, `String`, a leaf type, `Arc<Mailbox>`, an object: a const assertion the compiler runs says so for a plain name that turns out to be an object), a function with two type parameters; in the schema a `generic` label that does not describe its definition (the name is not `of<Type>`, the argument is not a record or an enum of the schema, a constructor or port method carries a label) or definitions that share one `of` but are not one function with one type replaced (a different parameter list, `is_async`, `takes_ctx`, `inferred` flag, parameter name or type shape with the names erased)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `generic(U = [..])` on `wrong_parameter`, which has no type parameter `U` | the list says which types a type parameter of the function is instantiated with; `wrong_parameter` declares `T` | write `generic(T = [Todo, Note])` |
| `generic(T = [..])` on `no_parameter`, which has no type parameter `T` | the list says which types a type parameter of the function is instantiated with; `no_parameter` declares none | remove `generic(..)`, or add the type parameter |
| the list of `T` on `empty` is empty | a generic function crosses once per listed type; with no type it would not cross at all | list at least one type, `generic(T = [Todo])`, or remove `#[undra::api]` if the function is not for the platforms |
| `Todo` is listed twice for `T` on `repeated` | each listed type becomes one function, `repeated<Todo>`, and two functions cannot share that name | remove one of them |
| `Vec<Todo>` cannot be listed for `T` on `unnamed` | each instantiation is presented under the name of its type (`draft(Todo.self)` in Swift, `draft(Todo::class)` in Kotlin, `draft("Todo")` in TypeScript), so a listed type is a value type declared with `#[undra::api]`: a record, an enum, a newtype or a named instantiation | list the element type and write `Vec<T>` in the signature, or give the type a name: `#[undra::api] pub struct Todos(pub Vec<Todo>);` |
| `u32` cannot be listed for `T` on `unnamed` | each instantiation is presented under the name of its type (`draft(Todo.self)` in Swift, `draft(Todo::class)` in Kotlin, `draft("Todo")` in TypeScript), so a listed type is a value type declared with `#[undra::api]`: a record, an enum, a newtype or a named instantiation | list the element type and write `Vec<T>` in the signature, or give the type a name: `#[undra::api] pub struct Todos(pub Vec<Todo>);` |

### `E0073` an `infinite` query that does not meet ADR-043's shape: no `item_key` or one that names no field of the rows, no or more than one `#[undra(cursor)]` parameter, a cursor that is not `Option<C>` or is in the key, a success type that is not `Page<T, C>`, rows that are not a record

Raised by macros, schema validation.

an `infinite` query (ADR-043) that is not a list of records with a cursor: no `item_key`, or one that names no field of the rows; no or more than one `#[undra(cursor)]` parameter, a cursor that is not `Option<C>` or is part of the `key`; a success type that is not `Page<T, C>` (with `C` the cursor's type) or rows that are not a record; `item_key`, `refetch_pages` or `persist_pages` without `infinite`, `persist_pages` without `persist`, `#[undra(cursor)]` on a query that is not `infinite`; in the schema an `infinite` mutation or a `returns` that is not `Vec<T>` of a record with the `item_key` field: the handle shows the pages as one list keyed by a field of its rows, and each page is asked for with the cursor the previous one returned

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the infinite query `no_cursor` has no `#[undra(cursor)]` parameter | the core asks for each page with the cursor the previous one returned: exactly one parameter carries it, `None` for the first page | mark one parameter `#[undra(cursor)] cursor: Option<String>` (or the cursor type your server uses) |
| the infinite query `two_cursors` has 2 `#[undra(cursor)]` parameters | the core asks for each page with the cursor the previous one returned: exactly one parameter carries it, `None` for the first page | mark one parameter `#[undra(cursor)] cursor: Option<String>` (or the cursor type your server uses) |
| the cursor `cursor` of `not_an_option` is `String`, not an `Option<C>` | the cursor is `None` for the first page and the previous page's `next` after it | write `#[undra(cursor)] cursor: Option<String>`, or another value type for the cursor your server uses |
| the cursor `cursor` is in the `key` of the infinite query `in_the_key` | every page of one list shares one cache entry, so the cursor, which differs per page, cannot be part of its key | remove the placeholder from `key`; the key holds the parameters that distinguish lists |
| `#[undra(cursor)]` on `cursor`, which is not a parameter of an `infinite` query | the cursor is how an infinite query asks for its next page; an ordinary query has no pages | remove the attribute, or add `infinite` and `item_key = ".."` to the query |
| `item_key = "idd"` of the infinite query `typo` names no field of `Post` | `item_key` names the field of the rows that identifies them, and `Post` has the fields `id`, `title` | write the name of one of those fields as `item_key` |

### `E0074` the impl block of a generic object that is not for the type with its own type parameters, each exactly once, or a method of a generic object with type parameters of its own (ADR-058; addition)

Raised by macros.

the impl block of a generic object (ADR-058) that is not for the type with its own type parameters, each exactly once (`impl<T> Cache<Vec<T>>`, `impl<T> Cache<T, Todo>`, a parameter applied twice or not at all), or a method of a generic object that has type parameters of its own, with or without a `generic(..)` list: an instantiation is one class on each platform, and a second level of generics would multiply every one of them

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the impl block of the generic object `Cache` is for `Cache<Vec<T>>` | a generic object is instantiated by naming its type arguments (`pub type TodoCache = Cache<Todo>;`), so its block is for the type with its own parameters, each exactly once | write `impl<T> Cache<T>` and put the type you meant in the methods' types |
| the impl block of the generic object `Pair` is for `Pair<A, Todo>` | a generic object is instantiated by naming its type arguments (`pub type TodoPair = Pair<Todo, Tag>;`), so its block is for the type with its own parameters, each exactly once | write `impl<A, B> Pair<A, B>` and put the type you meant in the methods' types |
| the impl block of the generic object `Twin` is for `Twin<A, A>` | a generic object is instantiated by naming its type arguments (`pub type TodoTwin = Twin<Todo, Tag>;`), so its block is for the type with its own parameters, each exactly once | write `impl<A, B> Twin<A, B>` and put the type you meant in the methods' types |
| `generic(..)` on `convert`, a method of the generic object `Box2` | an instantiation of a generic object is one class on each platform; a type parameter on a method would multiply every instantiation by it | make the parameter a type parameter of the object and name it in the alias, or write the method for a concrete type |
| generic parameter `U` on `map`, a method of the generic object `Box2` | an instantiation of a generic object is one class on each platform; a type parameter on a method would multiply every instantiation by it | make the parameter a type parameter of the object and name it in the alias, or write the method for a concrete type |

## The command line

### `C0001` no `undra.toml` from `start` up to the filesystem root

Raised by `undra`.

not inside an Undra project: no `undra.toml` from the working directory up to the filesystem root

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no undra.toml found in <dir> or any parent directory | this command works on an Undra project, and a project is the directory that holds undra.toml | run it inside a project, point at one with `-C <dir>`, or create one with `undra init <name>` |

### `C0002` a configuration or schema file is unusable

Raised by `undra`.

`undra.toml` or a schema file cannot be read or has a value the CLI cannot use

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <dir>/undra.toml: line 2: `name` in [project] is an integer but must be a string | the file drives the build, so a value the CLI cannot understand would make it guess | write it as a string, for example `name = "text"` |

### `C0003` a tool is not installed

Raised by `undra`.

a tool the command needs is not installed or not on `PATH`

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cargo` was not found | reading the core crate needs `cargo`, and it is not on your PATH | install Rust with rustup: https://rustup.rs (then open a new terminal) run `undra doctor` to check the rest of the toolchain |

### `C0004` a build tool exited with a failure

Raised by `undra`.

a build tool ran and failed; its own output follows the diagnostic

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cargo metadata` failed while reading the core crate (exit status: 101) | the tool's own output above says what it objected to; Undra cannot continue without its result | fix the problem the tool reported and run the command again; `undra doctor` checks the toolchain |

### `C0005` the core crate is missing, or is not an Undra core

Raised by `undra`.

the core crate is missing, or is not an Undra core

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the core crate `c0005-core` does not depend on Undra | without the `undra` crate there are no `#[undra::api]` items to describe, and the schema would be empty | add `undra = "0.1"` to the core's [dependencies] (or a `path` to your Undra checkout) |

### `C0006` the schema could not be extracted from the built core

Raised by `undra`.

the schema could not be extracted from the built core

The command prints this diagnostic with the details of the failure that caused it.

### `C0007` the schema cannot be turned into bindings (bindgen diagnostics)

Raised by `undra`.

the schema cannot be turned into bindings (the E0001, E0005, E0006, E0010, E0011, E0031, E0050, E0051, E0052 and E0072 diagnostics of schema validation follow)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the schema cannot be turned into bindings (1 problem) | the public surface of the core has to be expressible in Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript, and these items are not | change the items named below in the core (each message says what to do), then run `undra bindgen` again |

### `C0008` the command would overwrite something it must not

Raised by `undra`.

`undra init` or `undra adopt` would write into a directory that already has files in it

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <dir>/taken already exists and is not empty | `undra init` creates a new project and will not write into a directory that has files in it | choose another name, or another parent with `--dir`; to add Undra to an existing app use `undra adopt <dir>/taken` |

### `C0009` an argument is unusable

Raised by `undra`.

an argument has a value the command cannot use

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HEAD` has no `schema.json` | `--against` compares the schema file committed at the ref with the one in the working tree, so the ref has to have it | commit the schema file there (`undra schema export -o schema.json`), name another file, or compare two files (`undra schema diff old.json new.json`) |
| `my app` cannot be a project name: it contains characters other than ASCII letters, digits, `-` and `_` | the name becomes a Cargo package (`<name>-core`), a Swift module and a Kotlin package, which are stricter than file names | choose a name like `todo-app` or `acme_notes` you can still call the folder anything: `undra init my-app --dir <parent>` |

### `C0010` an I/O operation failed

Raised by `undra`.

a file or directory operation failed

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| could not create <dir>/afile/demo: Not a directory (os error 20) | the command needs to read or write this path and the operating system refused | check that the path exists and that you may access it, then run the command again |

### `C0011` the Rust toolchain lacks a compilation target

Raised by `undra`.

the Rust toolchain lacks a compilation target the build needs

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the Rust target `wasm32-unknown-unknown` is not installed | building for this platform needs the standard library compiled for it, and rustup has not installed it | rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown |

### `C0012` the platform is not available on this machine

Raised by `undra`.

the platform is not available on this machine

The command prints this diagnostic with the details of the failure that caused it.

### `C0013` the dev server failed to start or crashed

Raised by `undra`.

the dev server failed to start or crashed

The command prints this diagnostic with the details of the failure that caused it.

### `C0014` the project's Undra does not match: the core's comes from elsewhere, or it is newer

Raised by `undra`.

the core and the project disagree about where Undra comes from, or the project is on a newer Undra than this `undra` (`undra upgrade` moves a project forward only)

| What you see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| core/Cargo.toml pins Undra at tag v999.0.0, newer than this undra (<version>) | `undra upgrade` moves a project forward only, and a CLI older than the project's runtimes would generate bindings they do not match (ahead is <dir>/ahead) | update this `undra` first (`curl -fsSL https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/install.sh \| sh`, or `cargo install --locked --force --git https://github.com/shreypdev/undra undra-cli` if you installed it with cargo) and run `undra upgrade` again |
| undra.toml says Undra is at /somewhere/else, but the core's `undra` dependency is at <repo> | the library Undra ships is built from the same Undra as the core, and the platform runtimes come from `[undra] path`; if they differ, the core and the apps would speak different wire formats | make them agree: set `path` of the core's `undra` dependency and `[undra] path` in undra.toml to the same checkout (or remove `[undra] path` to use released runtimes) |

## Runtime messages

The JavaScript runtime (`@undra/runtime`) throws and logs these. Its **production build** (what `vite build`, webpack in production mode and anything else that asks for neither the `development` nor the `react-native` condition resolve) says a code, the values and a link instead of a sentence, so a page does not carry the prose of an error whose class, `kind` and fields it already has: `T0017: callSync, remote; see https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html#T0017`. Its **development build** (Vite's dev server, Vitest, React Native) says the sentence. Both throw the same classes with the same `kind` and fields; only `message` differs, so nothing a program can branch on changes. Text the runtime hands on as data, the field of a port's typed error (which the core receives) and a WebSocket close frame's reason (which the peer receives), is not a message: it is the same sentence in both builds. Codes are never reused.

### The T codes (166)

The sentence is what the development build says; `{0}`, `{1}`, ... are the values the production message lists, in that order.
